question.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

Letting $\theta =4x,$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)={cos}^{2}⁡(4x)-{sin}^{2}⁡(4x).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /16}({cos}^{2}⁡(4x)-{sin}^{2}⁡(4x))\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /16}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /16} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\cdot \frac{\pi }{16})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
